### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce4d8c7d7486fa5ab1fe4f33066a273c59a6b9f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea0a2b37addb3d4fb36e537a14048f4aac46e5ad` — the merge of head `cb1a47e97e1b9c4654b612702422ca53d1e38723` into base `ce4d8c7d7486fa5ab1fe4f33066a273c59a6b9f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea0a2b37addb3d4fb36e537a14048f4aac46e5ad && git checkout ea0a2b37addb3d4fb36e537a14048f4aac46e5ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ce4d8c7d7486fa5ab1fe4f33066a273c59a6b9f7 cb1a47e97e1b9c4654b612702422ca53d1e38723 && git checkout -B drift-repro ce4d8c7d7486fa5ab1fe4f33066a273c59a6b9f7 && git merge --no-ff cb1a47e97e1b9c4654b612702422ca53d1e38723

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce4d8c7d7486fa5ab1fe4f33066a273c59a6b9f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czzx9dtSEm3jWWL9c3

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK — held for a ruling, no dev work yet** at head `cb1a47e97e1b9c4654b612702422ca53d1e38723` (Fixes #37486). Full read · 2026-11-27T01:57Z

The code does what the card asks, and the tests prove it. It may not land on this head, for two reasons: it contradicts ADR-0160 as it stands, and the change it makes opens a question the ADR answered the other way elsewhere. That question needs a ruling on the governed ADR text before this PR or the amendment moves.

## 1. It contradicts the ADR that is on main

ADR-0160 D3, "A `related` child that this caller is not served is left out": "Nothing of the child is read, its definition included." This head reads `door.publishedObjectDefinitionOf(entry.object)` for exactly that child (`record-context-tools.ts`, step 4a). The PR body carries a replacement sentence for #37386's ADR edit, but no PR for #37386 is open (the card is `pm:dispatched`, claimed at 00:33Z). `docs/adr/**` is governed: its text changes only on the approver's record. Landing code that breaks the binding text before that record would put main against a governed rule whose approval could go the other way. **Answer to the area's point (1): #37751 waits for the ADR-0160 amendment to merge.**

## 2. The amendment is not a wording fix: it trades away an existence guarantee

The card's premise is D1: "the tool answer says nothing about" an author defect. D3 and the record tools say the opposite for this exact pair:

- ADR-0160 Context, quoting `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts#notRecordedMembersOf`: "an object or a field the caller's schema does not show is answered exactly as one that does not exist".
- ADR-0160 D3, on a lookup left unexpanded: "telling the two apart takes a read the caller cannot make, so both render alike."

On main, a child the stack does not define and a child this caller is not served render alike (both: section left out, one `not_visible` note). This head tells them apart with a read the caller cannot make: the published definition. A caller who knows a pack's `related` object names now learns, from note or no note, whether an object it is not served exists. The two-caller test proves the answer does not depend on who asks. It does not prove the answer reveals nothing to the one who asks. The aggregated note blurs this when other material is also hidden, but in the plain case (one hidden child, nothing else withheld) it is a clean yes/no.

Whether an ordinary caller can read a pack's `related` names is not settled here, and that changes how much this matters. Either way, it is the approver's trade, not a wording edit:

- **A. Keep main's behaviour.** Both render alike. The typo stays visible to its author through `os validate` (`ai-context-object-unknown`), which is D1's "reported on author surfaces". The ADR gains one sentence saying D1's "says nothing" yields to the render-alike rule here, and #37486 closes as by design. This PR closes unmerged.
- **B. Adopt this PR.** The amendment must name the existence signal it gives, not only "nothing of the definition is carried". Then #37751 lands after it.

L1-a recommends **A**: it keeps the existence guarantee ADR-0106 and the record tools hold everywhere else, and the author already has the typo reported where authors look. The seat takes this to the maintainer.

## Everything else holds (for B)

**Shape and gates.** `l1-face --pr 37751`: one flag, not a gap. `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts` is the only runtime file, and runtime's `files` is `dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md`, so nothing runtime ships moves. Check-runs at cb1a47e97e: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` success. Not governed. Runtime typecheck and `check:type-check-debt` left to CI: they are green on this head, so that holds (area point 2).

**Clause-②.** `no` is the right line. The tool's notes for one author-defect case change; no accept set, export or wire shape moves (`not_visible` already exists). So no L2 face is touched, and no tier read is owed. The card's "with the L2" is answered by this read: the substance it was guarding is section 2 above.

**Tests.** Red on main shown (1 failed of 30 on the real-kernel file, the expected `not_visible` vs `[]`). Green: bridge 30/30, package 180/180. The ablation of `if (published) hidden = true` goes red. The pins cover both doors, two callers, the defined-but-unserved control, and a throwing published read (coded refusal unnamed, failure fails). The harness extension instead of a new file is the shared-harness rule: accepted.

**Changeset.** The sentences hold against the diff, under B.
